messages.subject: Preventing freezing tables/plots that come from invalidate later and long calculation chains
messages.subject_clean: Preventing freezing tables/plots that come from invalidate later and long calculation chains
messages.body_plain:
Is there an option or work around in Shiny that can prevent the temporarily freezing/'white out' of tables and base R plots while calculations are being updated?

I would like to use shiny to update live time series plots and tables ideally every couple of seconds, but it is visually unappealing to see the plots and tables "freeze" temporarily while they wait for dependencies to compute that are time consuming (a second or two, for example).

One work around for plots I've found is to use ggvis for updating plots; they don't "Freeze"/'white out' while waiting for time consuming computations and just update, but I would like to use renderTable, renderDataTable and renderPlot, all which seem to have this freezing issue.

I would rather just see the plots/tables update once the calculations are completed with no freezing while waiting for the intermediate calculations.

Below is a minimal example that imitates the problem if you run the app:

library(shiny)

compute_seconds <- 1.5

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

    values <- reactive({
        invalidateLater(input$delay * 1000, session)
        data <- mtcars[sample(1:20),]
        Sys.sleep(compute_seconds) # This sleep represents some intensive calculation that takes a few seconds to crunch through

        data
    })

    output$showtable <- renderTable({
        values()
    })

})

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

    sidebarLayout(
        sidebarPanel(
            sliderInput("delay", "Delay (secs):",
                        min = 1, max = 30, value = 4, step = 0.5)
        ),

        mainPanel(
            h5("Don't want to see this table freeze/'white out' when output$showtable is invalidated and is waiting on a long computation"),
            tableOutput("showtable")
        )
    )
))

runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))

--------------
I asked a related question about this a year ago but haven't come up with a clean solution.  This kind of issue is also hard to describe and 'search for' on the web, if a solution already exists and I've missed it ...
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/freezing/shiny-discuss/DvSwDpgopXI/R7YAyIpK9qIJ

messages.body_plain:
Hi, I'm running shiny_0.12.2, R 3.2.2, and I have a datatable rendered as follows:

output$ixpivot <- renderDataTable(rv$data() ,options= rv$options)

I'd like an actionButton with id = "mapcolors" to trigger a change in the data being used for the DataTables, as well as options.

piv_data2 <- ix_mapped()[[1]]
hidecols <- ix_mapped()[[2]]

options.pivot <- reactive(list(dom = 'lfrtp', scrollX = "100%", "border-collapse" = "collapse",
                               pageLength = 15, lengthMenu = append(c(1:25), 50)
                               ,createdRow = I(row_names_format)
                               ,language = list(lengthMenu = "Display: _MENU_")))
options.mapped <- reactive(list(dom = 'lfrtp', scrollX = "100%"
                          ,"border-collapse" = "collapse"
                          ,pageLength = 10, lengthMenu = append(c(1:25), 50)
                          ,createdRow = I(color_mapping), columnDefs = hidecols
                          ,language = list(lengthMenu = "Display: _MENU_")))

rv <- reactiveValues(data = ix_pivot, options = options.pivot)

observeEvent(input$mapcolors, { rv$data <- piv_data2 })
observeEvent(input$mapcolors, { rv$options <- options.mapped })

Here, ix_mapped()[[2]] refers to a function that hides half the columns in the dataset, stored as ix_mapped()[[1]].

When I run the app, the table renders. I click the actionButton, and the new dataset piv_data2 is appears as the table - so the button works. However, the options are not updated with options.mapped, despite the fact that I've run the same options separately using options = options.mapped with no problems. Please let me know if you need any more information, any guidance would be appreciated!

-Muggy

My workaround at the moment is just to copy the code into the project directory for the app and reference it (source it) there - but this backward step is not very nice and will someday lead to a version control error.

Any advice on the 'normal workflow' for deploying an app with a private package?  And more in general, is there recommended comprehensive documentation on the whole shiny ecosystem and shiny workflow?  There's lots of snippets of great documentation, but I'm looking for the 'manual'.

Thanks - Giles

messages.subject: Re: non-public code - do I need to make a local copy for deployment?
messages.subject_clean: non-public code - do I need to make a local copy for deployment?
messages.body_plain:
GIles,

shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> supports installing private packages from GitHub assuming two things: 1) you installed the package using `devtoos::install_github`, 2) you've linked your shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> account to GitHub and enabled 'private repository access' in the dashboard. Using this method, when you deploy your app we will download the package directly from GitHub.

We currently don't support similar functionality for bitbucket, but this is something we coud look at adding if we get lot of requests for it. It would probably work identically to the way GitHub works.

-Andy

messages.subject: Q: serving deeply nested subdirs of .Rmd files?
messages.subject_clean: Q: serving deeply nested subdirs of .Rmd files?
messages.body_plain:
I have a directory tree of independent shiny-runtime .Rmd files, and because there's no auto-indexing with directory URLs, there's an index.Rmd in each directory that auto-builds a page of links for that directory (and subdirs). However, this only works for the top level directory, all other subdirectories fail to completely load, because the relative URLs for, e.g. "shared/shiny.css" cannot be found.  In other words:

server.name:3838/top/subdir/shared/shiny <http://server.name:3838/top/subdir/shared/shiny>.css -- exists
server.name:3838/top/subdir/subsubdir/shared/ <http://server.name:3838/top/subdir/subsubdir/shared/>shiny.css -- not found

even though server.name/top/subdir/subsubdir/foo.Rmd <http://server.name/top/subdir/subsubdir/foo.Rmd> does seem to trigger the shiny runtime process.

Any shiny-server config I can do to cleanly serve these URLs?

for now, I implemented a mod_rewrite rule to catch all such subsubdir/ requests, and reroute them to subdir/, but it's a fragile solution that depends on hardcoding the various "shared", "__assets__", etc.

thanks,
-Aaron

P.S. the barebones index.Rmd file I'm using in each subdir looks like this:

---

title: "Directory Listing"

runtime: shiny

output: html_document

---

## Available Pages:

```{r, echo=FALSE}

renderUI({

  pages <- dir(pattern=".Rmd$", full.names = T, recursive = T, include.dirs = T)

  pages <- sub("^\\.\\/", "", pages) # remove leading ./

  pages <- pages[pages != "index.Rmd"]

  basedir <- getwd()

  basedir <- sub("/srv/shiny-server/", "", basedir)

  links <- sprintf("http://server.name:3838/%s/%s", basedir, pages)

  pages <- sub("\\.Rmd$", "", pages)

  tags$ul(tagList(lapply(1:length(pages), function (i) { tags$li(tags$a(pages[i], href=links[i])) })))

})

```

messages.subject: renderPlot Parameters Processing Order
messages.subject_clean: renderPlot Parameters Processing Order
messages.body_plain: For renderPlot, the width and height parameters are processed before expr is. If I made a reactive expression for calculating it, I would need to copy some preliminary table filtering code twice, since when the reactive expression is called for width or height, it can't simply get variables referring to the filtered data table from renderPlot's expression, because the expression is not the parent environment in that case. Could renderPlot evaluate expr first, which would allow users to put the dimensions into the global environment and easily refer to them for width and height, if both of them were processed after expr ? Calling the reactive function twice is also unsuitable, for example, if it pops up a modal dialog message because all the of code was copied into the reactive expression, including the table subsetting code, which depends on at least one table row being selected, otherwise popping up an error message in a modal. If it were inside the reactive expression, it would annoyingly pop up twice to the user.

messages.subject: Re: renderPlot Parameters Processing Order
messages.subject_clean: renderPlot Parameters Processing Order
messages.body_plain:
The table filtering code should also be a reactive expression. And also, if a reactive expression is called twice without an intervening change to its reactive dependencies, then the second call will not cause the reactive expression code to be executed, because reactive expressions cache their results.

There's no way expr can execute before width/height. The graphics device must be initialized to the correct width/height before plotting code can execute.

messages.body_plain:
Is there a way to run apps on shiny-server one at a time?  I am currently running 5 apps on a server using Docker and the instructions here: https://gist.github.com/wch/411e2953f0258a72b9e0 but the apps occasionally fail.  I tried adding app_init_timeout and app_idle_timeout to the config file but it still fails.  I think this failure may be due to network calls within the shiny apps which may be blocking network access for the rest of Shiny Server of Docker to run.

I'd like to add into the shiny-server.sh bash script a loop that checks to make sure a given app is running correctly, and if not, to rerun it.  Since it is often the case if I try running all the apps that a few will work and a couple won't, it might be difficult to run this loop running all the apps at once, especially as I add more apps to the Docker container.  So, does anyone know if there is a way to only run one app at a time so that I can add this call to the loop in the bash script I will create?

Thanks for any help.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server global variables
messages.body_plain:
It would be conceivable to use another interprocess communication mechanism, like shared memory. But I don't know of any such mechanism today. Also, if you have writes happening simultaneously, you need to worry about two processes interleaving their writes which would end up causing the file to be corrupted. You can deal with this I believe, by not writing directly to the file, but by writing to a temp file in the same directory, then deleting the file and renaming the temp file to the permanent file name.

Ramnath Vaidyanathan offered this advice, which worked: My code had two problems: first, I had an extra comma after "value=x", and second, I needed to add the HTML "p" tag to address the fat that "textOutput" is a client-side function that is not to be used on the server-side.

Here is revised code for the server side:

tabs <- lapply(input$id,function(x){
  tabPanel(
   title = paste0(x,'_Tab'),
   h3(paste0('Tab showing:',x)),

   p(paste("The car you selected:", x,"has", mtcars[x,"cyl"], "cylinders")),   value=x
  )
})

This issue is resolved!

messages.subject: Re: Filter one selectInput based on selection from another selectInput?

messages.body_plain:
Solution:
library(shiny)
##
ui <- shinyUI({
  sidebarPanel(

    htmlOutput("brand_selector"),
    htmlOutput("candy_selector"))

})
##
server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  candyData <- read.table(
    text = "Brand       Candy
    Nestle      100Grand
    Netle       Butterfinger
    Nestle      Crunch
    Hershey's   KitKat
    Hershey's   Reeses
    Hershey's   Mounds
    Mars        Snickers
    Mars        Twix
    Mars        M&Ms",
    header = TRUE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  output$brand_selector <- renderUI({

    selectInput(
      inputId = "brand",
      label = "Brand:",
      choices = as.character(unique(candyData$Brand)),
      selected = "Nestle")

  })

  output$candy_selector <- renderUI({

    available <- candyData[candyData$Brand == input$brand, "Candy"]

    selectInput(
      inputId = "candy",
      label = "Candy:",
      choices = unique(available),
      selected = unique(available)[1])

  })

})
##
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Issue with Selectize Input within a draggable absolute panel in IE 11
messages.subject_clean: Issue with Selectize Input within a draggable absolute panel in IE 11
messages.body_plain:
In my app, I am using a draggable absolute panel. On the panel is a selectinput created using renderUI.

Using chrome, I have no issues. However, when our clients use Internet Explorer (11.0.9600.18015), and they try and scroll down within the input, the mouse becomes locked to the panel. Moving the mouse brings the panel with it. "Unclicking" does not work, and the only way I have gotten out of it is by right clicking and clicking elsewhere.

Is this a known bug with IE 11? We have also tested on IE 9 and there are no issues.

The following is a reproducible example:

ui.R
shinyUI(navbarPage("Leaflet App", id="nav",
                   tabPanel("Interactive map",
                            absolutePanel(id = "controls", fixed = TRUE,
                                              draggable = TRUE, top = 100, left = "auto", right = 20, bottom = "auto",
                                              width = 400, height = "auto",
                                              h2("Select Province"),
                                              br(),
                                              uiOutput("state_province_select")
                                )
                            )
)
)

server.R
shinyServer (
  function(input, output) {
    output$state_province_select <- renderUI({
      selectchoices <- c("Prince Edward Island","Ontario",
                         "Prince Edward Island1","Ontario1",
                         "Prince Edward Island2","Ontario2",
                         "Prince Edward Island3","Ontario3")
      selectlabel <- "Province"
      choiceselected <- "Prince Edward Island"
      selectInput("state_province_select",paste("Select ",selectlabel,":"),
                  choices = selectchoices, selected = choiceselected)
    })
  }
)

Try in IE 11, open the selectize input, and try and scroll down. Your mouse should immediately become stuck

messages.body_plain:
I haven't tried running your code, but I think the problem is that you're not backtick-ing the `data-toggle` and `data-target` attributes.  It's not a shiny problem, it just has to do with legal names in R. Using a dash inside a name is "not valid" so you need to surround it with backticks.  Same reason as why you can't run
my-var <- 5
but you can create a similar variable by surrounding it with backticks
`my-var` <- 5

It's not what mbh was referring to, but you can load data just once by putting it at the top of server.R. See "Objects visible across all sessions" on this page: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

If that's taking too long, if possible you should do whatever data massaging/transformation/aggregating/etc. outside of the Shiny app, and save the results as an .Rds file using saveRDS(), and load the data at the top of server.R using readRDS().

messages.body_plain:
Cole,

MySQL users are restricted to a particular host. You'll likely need to update your user record in MySQL to allow connections from any host. This is typically done by creating a user with a wildcard host and granting them privileges.

CREATE USER 'my-user'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'my-password';
GRANT ALL ON mydatabase.* TO 'my-user'@'%';

-Andy

Thanks for your suggestion! I think I'm doing the global data loading already (see my codes below). The data is stored with save() as a .RData file and load in outside of the shinyServer function. However, I'm not seeing the timing difference on the subsequent session, even on the same browser (Chrome) instance.

Thanks!
Wen

library(shiny)

# place the setup code here. they will be run just once when the app was invoked
library(lattice)

# Reading the search output. This is where the data loading occure
load("PD_lf.RData");

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

# render codes
  });

  output$distPlot3 <- renderPrint({

    ctable(lf$psm5[,c(input$param_y3,"Digestion")]);

  });

})

On Thursday, October 15, 2015 at 12:15:27 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> It's not what mbh was referring to, but you can load data just once by putting it at the top of server.R. See "Objects visible across all sessions" on this page: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html
>
> If that's taking too long, if possible you should do whatever data massaging/transformation/aggregating/etc. outside of the Shiny app, and save the results as an .Rds file using saveRDS(), and load the data at the top of server.R using readRDS().
>
> On Thu, Oct 15, 2015 at 6:38 AM Wen Yu <wyu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi, can you elaborate on what you need to do to "load the data in global R"? Is it something you can do in 'server.R' or on the Shiny server side? I'm desperately looking for a solution to improve the data loading. It's killing the user experience!
> >
> > Thanks!
> > Wen Yu
> >
> >
> > On Friday, May 29, 2015 at 5:29:11 AM UTC-4, Matthieu wrote:
> > > In my case, it's working as I want to. I put data loading in global.R and launch the app, it lasts 45 seconds.
> > > Then i'm connecting the app through another computer and it's immediate, I don't have to wait 45 seconds again.

> > > Le vendredi 29 mai 2015 09:19:26 UTC+2, Mario Deng a écrit :
> > > >
> > > > Hey everyone,
> > > >
> > > > just as Joe mentioned, there is no solution, it just requires its time.
> > > >
> > > > Using an external DB (benchmarked Redis and MongoDB for my use case) is not feasible, both systems are way to slow. I kept going with data.table, keep everything in memory and accept some extra time during startup. Setting the timeout for an app to ~20h did the job in my case.
> > > >
> > > > Best,
> > > >
> > > > On Friday, May 29, 2015 at 9:06:09 AM UTC+2, Carlos Sánchez wrote:
> > > > > Hi Mario,
> > > > >
> > > > > Have you thought about putting your data in a database and pulling the data from it as you needed? I'm not really sure what your app does but in my case I needed to access 25GB of data. For my solution, I decided to go with Elasticsearch and then just query the DB to pull the data. It works really well and you avoid the loading issue as the data is always there via ELasticsearch. There are other options besides ES within R like MongoDB or Postgres so you can choose the one you like the most.

On Tuesday, September 22, 2015 at 4:32:48 AM UTC-7, Ted Mendum wrote:
>
> Thanks Joe, I've gotten it to work now, using your suggestions.  I hope you've been staying somewhere nice.  Ted
>
>
> On Friday, September 18, 2015 at 2:59:37 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > Sorry for the delay, I'm on vacation.
> >
> >   vals <- reactiveValues(
> >     keeprows = rep(TRUE, 12) #nrow(mydata()))
> >   )
> >
> > What's your intention with this code? Is keeprows supposed to stay up to date as mydata changes? Or is it supposed to just run a single time at startup? If so, at the time this code is running, are you sure mydata() is going to return something sensible (I suspect not as mydata requires a file upload)?
> >
> > I'll assume that you want to prepopulate keeprows each time a new file is uploaded. Then you'll do something like this:
> >
> > vals <- reactiveValues(
> >   keeprows = NULL
> > )
> > observe({
> >   vals$keeprows <- rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
> > })
> >
> > Also add this line to the beginning of the mydata reactive:
> >
> > validate(need(input$file, FALSE))
> >
> > The validate/need call will cause any code that calls mydata() to silently/cleanly abort if the file hasn't been uploaded yet (i.e. your outputs will be blank, without any error).
> >
> > The observer will cause keeprows to stay up to date.
> >
> > The one edge case you may still hit, is if an observer or renderXXX accesses vals$keeprows without first accessing mydata(). You can either check for NULL in those cases (or better yet, validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) ) or wrap the access to vals$keeprows in a reactive that calls validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) before returning vals$keeprows. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html for more on this powerful but unintuitive feature.
> >
> > On Wed, Sep 16, 2015 at 12:09 PM Ted Mendum <men...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Thanks, Joe.  Your explanation confirms my nascent understanding of how shiny is supposed to work.  I have changed the code below to adopt your suggestions--now it is the same as the example code but tweaked to include a fileInput ui.  Also, I dropped the library call to Cairo, which fails on my system and which I don't believe is important.
> > >
> > > Unfortunately, I get a new error when I run the code:  Error: Line starting '<!DOCTYPE html> ...' is malformed!  From googling a bit this seems to have something to do with R referencing webpages that don't exist.  I tried splitting the code into independent ui.R and server.R files, and that fixed the problem...no idea why.
> > >
> > > However, once the app runs I get a different error which seems to crop up all the time (perhaps because I don't understand reactivity completely):
> > >
> > >
> > > Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() :
> > >   Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)
> > >
> > > By experimentation, I discovered that the source of the error seems to be the statement assigning vals, and, more specifically, the command nrow(mydata()).  If I comment out nrow(mydata()) as shown below and stick in a number, no error occurs, and the app runs.  (Of course, there are problems with 12 not actually being the correct number of rows, but that's a side issue)
> > >
> > >  vals <- reactiveValues(
> > >     keeprows = rep(TRUE, 12) #nrow(mydata()))
> > >   )
> > >
> > >
> > > On the other hand, if I comment out the vals assignment completely, the rest of the script can't do its job and I get an error that I expect:
> > >
> > > Error in func() : object 'vals' not found
> > > Error in `[.data.frame`(mydata(), vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE) :
> > >   object 'vals' not found
> > >
> > >
> > > Any further insights?  My version of shiny is 0.12.2, by the way, and R version 3.1.2 (2014-10-31).
> > >
> > >
> > > Ted
> > >
> > > Revised code below:
> > > #########################################
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > library(shiny)
> > > library(ggplot2)
> > >
> > > ui <- fluidPage(
> > >   fluidRow(
> > >     column(width = 6,
> > >   fileInput("file", "Load File"),
> > >                     plotOutput("plot1", height = 350,
> > >
> > >                       click = "plot1_click",
> > >                       brush = brushOpts(
> > >                         id = "plot1_brush"
> > >                       )
> > >            ),
> > >            actionButton("exclude_toggle", "Toggle points"),
> > >            actionButton("exclude_reset", "Reset")
> > >     )
> > >   )
> > > )
> > >
> > > server <- function(input, output) {
> > >   mydata <- reactive({
> > >     if(!is.null(input$file)){
> > >
> > >       read.table(input$file$datapath, header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
> > >     }
> > >   })
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > >   # For storing which rows have been excluded
> > >   vals <- reactiveValues(
> > >     keeprows = rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
> > >   )
> > >
> > >   output$plot1 <- renderPlot({
> > >     mynames <- names(mydata())
> > >
> > >     # Plot the kept and excluded points as two separate data sets
> > >     keep    <- mydata()[ vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]
> > >     exclude <- mydata()[!vals$keeprows, , drop = FALSE]
> > >
> > >     ggplot(keep, aes_string(mynames[1], mynames[2])) +
> > >       geom_point() +
> > >       geom_smooth(method = lm, fullrange = TRUE, shape = 21, color = "black") +
> > >       geom_point(data = exclude, shape = 21, fill = NA, color = "black", alpha = 0.25)
> > >
> > >   })
> > >

> > > > What's your intention with this code? Is keeprows supposed to stay up to date as mydata changes? Or is it supposed to just run a single time at startup? If so, at the time this code is running, are you sure mydata() is going to return something sensible (I suspect not as mydata requires a file upload)?
> > > >
> > > > I'll assume that you want to prepopulate keeprows each time a new file is uploaded. Then you'll do something like this:
> > > >
> > > > vals <- reactiveValues(
> > > >   keeprows = NULL
> > > > )
> > > > observe({
> > > >   vals$keeprows <- rep(TRUE, nrow(mydata()))
> > > > })
> > > >
> > > > Also add this line to the beginning of the mydata reactive:
> > > >
> > > > validate(need(input$file, FALSE))
> > > >
> > > > The validate/need call will cause any code that calls mydata() to silently/cleanly abort if the file hasn't been uploaded yet (i.e. your outputs will be blank, without any error).
> > > >
> > > > The observer will cause keeprows to stay up to date.
> > > >
> > > > The one edge case you may still hit, is if an observer or renderXXX accesses vals$keeprows without first accessing mydata(). You can either check for NULL in those cases (or better yet, validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) ) or wrap the access to vals$keeprows in a reactive that calls validate(need(vals$keeprows, FALSE)) before returning vals$keeprows. See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/validation.html for more on this powerful but unintuitive feature.

messages.subject: Re: Implementing Shiny on squarespace website
messages.subject_clean: Implementing Shiny on squarespace website
messages.body_plain:
It's not possible to host Shiny apps directly on Squarespace hardware. Shiny apps require a running R process to do the calculations, and that's not something that Squarespace does (nor any other general purpose web host).

What you could maybe do is create a dashboard on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> and make an iframe on Squarespace that embeds the dashboard.

messages.subject: Re: Phonegap
messages.subject_clean: Phonegap
messages.body_plain:
I spent some time on this a while back. Here's what I recall from my investigating:
I think the idea is doable, but there are a few awkward hacks.
Some of the difficulties come from using a load-balanced system like Shiny Server Pro or ShinyApps.io. I think you'd be better off -- at least for a proof-of-concept -- connecting to a single-process model like Shiny Server Open Source.
PhoneGap Build <https://build.phonegap.com/> is a competent enough platform -- ingests PhoneGap projects and products iPhone/Android/Windows/whatever packages. It's one more thing to learn/distrust, so I don't know that I'd recommend it for your "Hello World," but once you're ready to actually bundle something for multiple platforms, it's pretty nice.
There are some really awkward bits around what to bundle and what not to bundle. The idea of PhoneGap, of course, is that you could save all your static assets within your application bundle and then only connect to a server when necessary. This becomes complicated with the various ways that Shiny presents static assets and allows packages to extend those sets of static assets. It's tough to make sure you have everything downloaded locally, so you're probably better off just loading the base HTML file remotely. I had a hard time convincing PhoneGap Build to do this, though it looks like it is possible to do in PhoneGap itself. Note that this becomes difficult with point 6.
The persistent connection assumption of Shiny is awkward for a mobile device. When the WebSocket connection drops (which I'm sure depends on the platform/phone), you get the familiar gray screen covering your app. This is pretty awkward and hard for an app to recover from.
PhoneGap works by referencing a phonegap.js file in the code that you write to expose the PhoneGap API. Then when you compile, it replaces that file with the version relevant to your targeted platform. This clashes with my simplifying suggestion in point 4, in that if you're loading all the files remotely, then you can't have the PhoneGap build process replace your phonegap.js file with the one you actually need on that platform. There are ways around this in PhoneGap I believe, but I couldn't get any working when trying to load the files from a remote URL.
You still need to write the JavaScript integration between the PhoneGap API and Shiny. I had one or two of these working just to prove the concept, but it's work to be done.
So it's certainly possible to create a mobile app that just shows a remote URL (like ShinyApps) but there's a big jump between that and integrating the PhoneGap API to actually use the phone's capabilities.

I'm certainly not a PhoneGap expert, so I may have missed something obvious, and I don't know how valuable I'd be as a resource moving forward beyond what I've outlined in the above points, but feel free to ask if you have particular questions and I'll see if I remember.

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Sorry to tack onto another user's question, but I'm trying to test the suitability of Shiny for a couple of projects and I'm trying to tackle a similar issue...

I read the linked article, but I'm not clear on something.  If I want an object (eg, the output of a SQL query against our data warehouse) to be persistent across sessions, I put it at the top of my code, outside the shinyServer function.  I assume this will be created the first time the server.R code runs.  But if it's persistent across sessions, when does it refresh?  If ever?  Is there some way to force a refresh?  If so, can I refresh against a schedule?

The data in our data warehouse refreshes on a daily basis.  So there is no point re-loading data large data sets each time a user runs a shiny app.  But at the same time, I don't want the data to be persistent over a period of days.  Is there a recommended way to handle this?

this is a cross post from the leaflet google grp but might be more fitting here as it concerns the R application,

I have a probably simple question to answer but I dont get it done. I use the R leaflet package for a mapping project and create a colorQuantile(...) with 5 Quantils. When I  use addLegend (...) I get a legend looking like

color a  0%-20%
color b 20%-40%
color c 40%-60%
color d 60%-80%
color e 80%-100%

What I want to achieve is changing the quantil percent labels into something like

color a "very low"
color b "low"
color c "average"
...

I tried the labels argument of addLegend() but had no success with changing these labels.

Any help would be appreciated!

Here is a (slightly abridged) copy of my code;

library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

data <- reactivePoll(100000, session,

            checkFunc = function() {
              if (difftime(Sys.time(), attr(sales,”TIMESTAMP"), units="mins") > 1) {
                return("Old")
              } else {
                return("Current")
              }
            },
            valueFunc = function() {
              sales <- read.csv(“Sales_Data.pip", header = TRUE, sep = "|", quote = "\"")
	      attr(sales, “TIMESTAMP”) <- Sys.time()
              summary <-
                summarise(
                  group_by(
                    sales,
                    y=as.integer(year(Sales_Date)),
                    m=as.integer(month(Sales_Date)),
                    o=Office,
                    p=as.character(Product)
                  ),
                  c=n_distinct(Sales_ID)
                )
              return(summary)
            })

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  output$mytable2 = renderDataTable({
    data()
  }

  output$plot1 = renderPlot({
    plot<-ggplot(data(), aes(x=m, y=c))+
      geom_bar(stat = "identity", colour='black', fill='#B1005D') +
      xlab(“Sales by Product“) +
      ylab("Month") +
      scale_x_discrete()+
      facet_wrap(~p) +
      theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 14))
    plot(plot)
  })
})

messages.subject: Re: Is file uploaded by fileInput stored in memory or disk?
messages.subject_clean: Is file uploaded by fileInput stored in memory or disk?
messages.body_plain:
the file is stored in a temp folder. the path is stored in
inFile$datapath
the data frame for this file is stored in memory as passed to the renderTable function. if you want a way to access this data frame, you can do this

myDataFrame <- reactive({

    inFile <- input$file1

    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)

    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
  })

 then call myDataFrame() whenever you want the data

messages.body_plain:
There's no "session" variable in scope where you're calling reactivePoll, since you're operating outside of any user session at that point. Try passing NULL instead.

The reason for passing a session is so the reactivePoll can automatically stop itself when the user session ends (i.e. that particular browser window navigates away or closes). Passing NULL will just keep the reactivePoll running until the R process exits, which is what you want in this case.

messages.subject_clean: Shiny server with bigger data - in memory
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Joe, that works perfectly.

I could see that the session variable wasn't in scope, but removing didn't work.  Passing NULL however, works nicely.

While it is a bit of a pain to have to code up the rules for the checkFunction, it's really nice having the ability to fine-tune the data caching frequency.

On Wednesday, 21 October 2015 20:25:41 UTC+11, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> There's no "session" variable in scope where you're calling reactivePoll, since you're operating outside of any user session at that point. Try passing NULL instead.
>
> The reason for passing a session is so the reactivePoll can automatically stop itself when the user session ends (i.e. that particular browser window navigates away or closes). Passing NULL will just keep the reactivePoll running until the R process exits, which is what you want in this case.
>
> On Tue, Oct 20, 2015 at 1:50 PM Nick Mead <naj...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Joe.  I've been playing around with reactivePoll but keep getting an error.  It looks like the data loads initially, but after the polling period, I get the following error;
> >
> > Error in thisFunc() : object 'session' not found
> >
> > Here is a (slightly abridged) copy of my code;
> >
> > library(shiny)
> > library(dplyr)
> > library(lubridate)
> >
> > data <- reactivePoll(100000, session,
> >
> >             checkFunc = function() {
> >               if (difftime(Sys.time(), attr(sales,”TIMESTAMP"), units="mins") > 1) {
> >                 return("Old")
> >               } else {
> >                 return("Current")
> >               }
> >             },
> >             valueFunc = function() {
> >               sales <- read.csv(“Sales_Data.pip", header = TRUE, sep = "|", quote = "\"")
> > 	      attr(sales, “TIMESTAMP”) <- Sys.time()
> >               summary <-
> >                 summarise(
> >                   group_by(
> >                     sales,
> >                     y=as.integer(year(Sales_Date)),
> >                     m=as.integer(month(Sales_Date)),
> >                     o=Office,
> >                     p=as.character(Product)
> >                   ),
> >                   c=n_distinct(Sales_ID)
> >                 )
> >               return(summary)
> >             })
> >
> >
> > shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
> >
> >   output$mytable2 = renderDataTable({
> >     data()
> >   }
> >
> >   output$plot1 = renderPlot({
> >     plot<-ggplot(data(), aes(x=m, y=c))+
> >       geom_bar(stat = "identity", colour='black', fill='#B1005D') +
> >       xlab(“Sales by Product“) +
> >       ylab("Month") +
> >       scale_x_discrete()+
> >       facet_wrap(~p) +
> >       theme(strip.text.x = element_text(size = 14))
> >     plot(plot)
> >   })
> > })
> >
> >
> > On Tuesday, 20 October 2015 18:15:17 UTC+11, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > Nick, you can try reactivePoll for this purpose:
> > > http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/reactivePoll.html
> > >
> > > On Mon, Oct 19, 2015 at 5:37 PM Nick Mead <naj...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Sorry to tack onto another user's question, but I'm trying to test the suitability of Shiny for a couple of projects and I'm trying to tackle a similar issue...
> > > >
> > > > I read the linked article, but I'm not clear on something.  If I want an object (eg, the output of a SQL query against our data warehouse) to be persistent across sessions, I put it at the top of my code, outside the shinyServer function.  I assume this will be created the first time the server.R code runs.  But if it's persistent across sessions, when does it refresh?  If ever?  Is there some way to force a refresh?  If so, can I refresh against a schedule?
> > > >
> > > > The data in our data warehouse refreshes on a daily basis.  So there is no point re-loading data large data sets each time a user runs a shiny app.  But at the same time, I don't want the data to be persistent over a period of days.  Is there a recommended way to handle this?
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Friday, 16 October 2015 03:15:27 UTC+11, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > > > > It's not what mbh was referring to, but you can load data just once by putting it at the top of server.R. See "Objects visible across all sessions" on this page: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html
> > > > >
> > > > > If that's taking too long, if possible you should do whatever data massaging/transformation/aggregating/etc. outside of the Shiny app, and save the results as an .Rds file using saveRDS(), and load the data at the top of server.R using readRDS().
> > > > >
> > > > > On Thu, Oct 15, 2015 at 6:38 AM Wen Yu <wyu...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > Hi, can you elaborate on what you need to do to "load the data in global R"? Is it something you can do in 'server.R' or on the Shiny server side? I'm desperately looking for a solution to improve the data loading. It's killing the user experience!
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Thanks!
> > > > > > Wen Yu
> > > > > >
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Friday, May 29, 2015 at 5:29:11 AM UTC-4, Matthieu wrote:
> > > > > > > In my case, it's working as I want to. I put data loading in global.R and launch the app, it lasts 45 seconds.
> > > > > > > Then i'm connecting the app through another computer and it's immediate, I don't have to wait 45 seconds again.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Le vendredi 29 mai 2015 09:19:26 UTC+2, Mario Deng a écrit :
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Hey everyone,
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > just as Joe mentioned, there is no solution, it just requires its time.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Using an external DB (benchmarked Redis and MongoDB for my use case) is not feasible, both systems are way to slow. I kept going with data.table, keep everything in memory and accept some extra time during startup. Setting the timeout for an app to ~20h did the job in my case.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Friday, May 29, 2015 at 9:06:09 AM UTC+2, Carlos Sánchez wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Hi Mario,
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Have you thought about putting your data in a database and pulling the data from it as you needed? I'm not really sure what your app does but in my case I needed to access 25GB of data. For my solution, I decided to go with Elasticsearch and then just query the DB to pull the data. It works really well and you avoid the loading issue as the data is always there via ELasticsearch. There are other options besides ES within R like MongoDB or Postgres so you can choose the one you like the most.

> > > > > > > > > Carlos

messages.subject_clean: Question for Shiny data file saving and loading
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have built an application that has an reactive input, and when the input changes, it calls a customized function X(), in which it saves a model to a RData file.
My question is, if I have two different clients that visit my app from their machine, when they change the input, will that RData file be stored/loaded on/from server side or locally?
If server side, then will it cause synchronizing issues? If client side, then what path should I define?

Here's some code for reference:

server <- function(input,output,session){
  model <- reactive({
    modelRes<-NA

      setProgress(message = "Updating Model...")

      #Model is saved in "ValueMatrix.RData" in this function TopicModelTrain(), e.g., save(model, file = "ValueMatrix.RData")
      TopicModelTrain(isolate({input$sparsity}),isolate({input$TFIDFfilterLevel}),0.9,TRUE,input$topicNum,isolate({input$newdatatrain}),testingData,20,10)

      load("ValueMatrix.RData")

        ......

    return(modelRes)
  })
  ......
}

Appreciate your help!

Also, another important reason is that, the training data might or might not be changed, which means user could at some point train a model with new data, or still use the previous model if no new data is coming.
We do not want to go through the training process every new session, because when original dataset is large, it might take a long time, and if no new data within a while, we could reuse the model if save to a file.

I guess it is probably a package version issue but any thoughts would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks

Iain

messages.body_plain:
This is a bit odd. Normally, packages from BioConductor do not have a `Repository:` field set in their DESCRIPTION; however, they do come with a `biocViews` field in their DESCRIPTION.

Can you copy the contents of that package's DESCRIPTION file here? You can get it with something like:

    readLines(system.file("DESCRIPTION", package = "ComplexHeatmap"))

We might need to check for `biocViews` before checking / validating the repository.

messages.subject: shiny website for people with disabilities? (tips for Section 508 compliance?)
messages.subject_clean: shiny website for people with disabilities? (tips for Section 508 compliance?)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
  I like and use shiny a lot to share results within the research group I am in. Now we want to release this shiny website as part of our research publication, and we are planning to do this for many more projects in our group.

  Has anyone here built shiny-based websites that are accessible to people with disabilities? Specifically shiny websites that are Section 508 compliant (which is a good design principle for a website, and also required by law in federal agencies that we are part of, and those outside including institutes funded by federal agencies; please see http://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/  http://www.508checker.com/what-is-508-compliance ).

  I understand that the level of interactivity in shiny could sometimes be irreconcilable with section 508, however the key is if a good-faith effort is put in to make the website accessible. For instance, is there any effort by the developers or workaround by users to address html tags such as "alt" tags for interactive images produced by shiny (please see here: http://www.hhs.gov/web/section-508/making-files-accessible/checklist/html/index.html for more on alt tags)?

Thanks,
Mani

messages.subject: Managing Users Gracefully
messages.subject_clean: Managing Users Gracefully
messages.body_plain:
So I'm interested in what the best way is to manage users using R Shiny Pro. Two topics:
Restricting logins per accounts gracefully
Closing idle connections gracefully
For #1. Can you use LDAP to query connections, or should I use a database to insert when new users log-in and query that? Then it would need to tell users to log-out from other connections in order to log-in (and/or enable them to log-out for the other connections).

For #2. We need to keep a value for app_idle_timeout because we have issues when two sessions with the same user are connected (also would have more issues once #1 is implemented...). I don't see a way to directly read and write the session's idle time but am I wrong? Ideally we could capture idle time and at a certain point initiate a pop-up that says "Would you like to continue your session? You have X seconds until your session will be closed". Then if they click continue the idle time is overridden. If their session is ended it should go to log-in screen with alternative text message saying "Your session ended, please log back in". Is it possible to display alternative text on the log-in screen at this juncture?

Thanks,

Chris

messages.subject_clean: Execute R code after renderUI()
messages.body_plain:
You almost had it. Progress$new() takes three arguments: session, min, and max. If you pass the session explicitly, it works.

You should also pass once=TRUE to session$onFlushed. Otherwise that same code will be executed every time some reactivity is triggered.

On Sat, Oct 24, 2015 at 9:26 PM Jonathan Keane <jke...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I've been struggling to find a way to ensure that a piece of long running code is executed after a particular user interface is rendered.
>
> I know this use is not quite what shiny was designed for, but I'm developing a survey-like interface that has a sequence of pages with user inputs on each one. What I would like is that after one specific set of UI elements is displayed, I would like a (sometimes long-running) segment of code to run, but only after the UI has renedred, and with a progress indicator, so that users can be inputting what they need to while the code is running.
>
> I have gotten this to work, but currently it involves a (very hacky!) use of a custom message to the client:
>
> output$page <- renderUI({
>   div([shiny tags])
> })
>
>
> session$onFlushed(function() {
>   session$sendCustomMessage(type="grabStimuliList", list(TRUE))
> })
>
> I have the message handler:
>
> Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('grabStimuliList',
> function(params){
> console.log(params);
> Shiny.onInputChange("grabStims", 1);
> });
>
>
>
> And above this, I have an observe event that acts
>
> observeEvent(input$grabStims, {
>     if(input$grabStims==1){
>       progress <- shiny::Progress$new()
>       progress$set(message = "Generating videos", value = 0)
>       [long running R code, with progress updating mechanisms]
>     }
>   })
>
>

> Error in public_bind_env$initialize(...) :

>
> It will run if I remove the progress code, but then there's no indication to the user of the progress.

messages.subject: Re: Managing Users Gracefully
messages.subject_clean: Managing Users Gracefully
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

For #1, am I understanding correctly that you want to restrict the global number of sessions a single user can have at once? If so, that's unfortunately not something that LDAP would be able to help with. You'd need to setup an extra system somewhere (could be as simple as a directory of files on your server or could be a whole web API) that would be able to track how many sessions each user currently has. You'd integrate with that system in your Shiny code by querying to see if the user should be allowed to open this new connection or not and kill the connection if not.

For #2, we unfortunately don't include this feature at the moment, but it is a request we've heard before and do plan to tackle. For the time being, however, you'd probably have to track the idle time yourself in JavaScript as you suggested, and you could disable the `app_idle_timeout` setting so you can just manage all of this on your own. I haven't stayed up-to-date on the various libraries people have put out there, but here's at least one that claims to be able to show alerts, if you're trying to minimize the amount of JS you have to write. https://github.com/AnalytixWare/ShinySky

Jeff

> > Closing idle connections gracefully

> >
> > For #2. We need to keep a value for app_idle_timeout because we have issues when two sessions with the same user are connected (also would have more issues once #1 is implemented...). I don't see a way to directly read and write the session's idle time but am I wrong? Ideally we could capture idle time and at a certain point initiate a pop-up that says "Would you like to continue your session? You have X seconds until your session will be closed". Then if they click continue the idle time is overridden. If their session is ended it should go to log-in screen with alternative text message saying "Your session ended, please log back in". Is it possible to display alternative text on the log-in screen at this juncture?
> >

Oh, if you're operating on a file, you don't want reactivePoll; you want reactiveFileReader, which implements checkFunc by consulting the last-modified-time of the file.

sales <- reactiveFileReader(1000, NULL, "Sales_Data.pip", read.csv, header = TRUE, sep = "|", quote = "\"")
data <- reactive({
  summarise(
    group_by(
      sales(),

      y=as.integer(year(Sales_Date)),
      m=as.integer(month(Sales_Date)),
      o=Office,
      p=as.character(Product)
    ),
    c=n_distinct(Sales_ID)
  )

})

And for completeness, if all your checkFunc is going to do is wait for a certain amount of time to expire, you don't even need reactivePoll. You can just use invalidateLater().

data <- reactive({

  sales <- read.csv(“Sales_Data.pip", header = TRUE, sep = "|", quote = "\"")

  summary <-
    summarise(
      group_by(
        sales,
        y=as.integer(year(Sales_Date)),
        m=as.integer(month(Sales_Date)),
        o=Office,
        p=as.character(Product)
      ),
      c=n_distinct(Sales_ID)
    )

  invalidateLater(60*1000, NULL)
  return(summary)
})

   tags$style(HTML(".radio label:first-child{font-weight:bold"))

However, this makes the first label of all radiobutton groups bold. I have several radiobutton groups and I only want one of the groups to be bold.
When I specify between groups using class and modify the above code to the class name (.rbutton1 instead of .radio) and use this line of code:
  tags$style(HTML(".rbutton1 .radio label:first-child{font-weight:bold"))
only labels from the specified radio button grouping are bold but all labels, not just the first label, are bold. In the example below, I want only "Zero" to be bold.

ui.R
library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Example"),
 tags$head(
   tags$style(HTML(".rbutton .radio label:first-child{font-weight:bold"))),

   mainPanel(
     tags$div(class="rbutton1", radioButtons("NumberSelect", "Select One", choices=c("Zero"="0","One"=1, "Two"=2, "Three"=3), selected="Zero")),
     tags$div(class="rbutton2", radioButtons("LetterSelect", "Select One", choices=c("A","B",C"), selected="A"))
    )
))

server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  renderText(NumberSelect())
})

On Mon, Oct 26, 2015 at 2:28 PM, Jeff Allen <jeff....@jdadesign.net> wrote:

> Hi Chris,
>
> For #1, am I understanding correctly that you want to restrict the global number of sessions a single user can have at once? If so, that's unfortunately not something that LDAP would be able to help with. You'd need to setup an extra system somewhere (could be as simple as a directory of files on your server or could be a whole web API) that would be able to track how many sessions each user currently has. You'd integrate with that system in your Shiny code by querying to see if the user should be allowed to open this new connection or not and kill the connection if not.
>
> For #2, we unfortunately don't include this feature at the moment, but it is a request we've heard before and do plan to tackle. For the time being, however, you'd probably have to track the idle time yourself in JavaScript as you suggested, and you could disable the `app_idle_timeout` setting so you can just manage all of this on your own. I haven't stayed up-to-date on the various libraries people have put out there, but here's at least one that claims to be able to show alerts, if you're trying to minimize the amount of JS you have to write. https://github.com/AnalytixWare/ShinySky
>
> Jeff
>
>
> On Friday, October 23, 2015 at 5:26:02 PM UTC-5, hol...@geocf.com wrote:
> > I guess I need to pass some new data around using JS: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/667555/detecting-idle-time-in-javascript-elegantly
> >
> > On Friday, October 23, 2015 at 5:24:13 PM UTC-5, hol...@geocf.com wrote:
> > > So I'm interested in what the best way is to manage users using R Shiny Pro. Two topics:

> > > Closing idle connections gracefully
> > > For #1. Can you use LDAP to query connections, or should I use a database to insert when new users log-in and query that? Then it would need to tell users to log-out from other connections in order to log-in (and/or enable them to log-out for the other connections).
> > >
> > > For #2. We need to keep a value for app_idle_timeout because we have issues when two sessions with the same user are connected (also would have more issues once #1 is implemented...). I don't see a way to directly read and write the session's idle time but am I wrong? Ideally we could capture idle time and at a certain point initiate a pop-up that says "Would you like to continue your session? You have X seconds until your session will be closed". Then if they click continue the idle time is overridden. If their session is ended it should go to log-in screen with alternative text message saying "Your session ended, please log back in". messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have built an application that has an reactive input, and when the input changes, it calls a customized function X(), in which it saves a model to a RData file.
My question is, if I have two different clients that visit my app from their machine, when they change the input, will that RData file be stored/loaded on/from server side or locally?
If server side, then will it cause synchronizing issues? If client side, then will it automatically save to client's machine?

Here's some code for reference:

Server.R
server <- function(input,output,session){
  model <- reactive({
    modelRes<-NA

      setProgress(message = "Updating Model...")

      #Model is saved in "ValueMatrix.RData" in this function TopicModelTrain(), e.g., save(model, file = "ValueMatrix.RData")
      TopicModelTrain(isolate({input$sparsity}),isolate({input$TFIDFfilterLevel}),0.9,TRUE,input$topicNum,isolate({input$newdatatrain}),testingData,20,10)

      load("ValueMatrix.RData")

        ......

    return(modelRes)
  })
  ......
}

topicmodelingTest.R

...if(!file.exists("trainedModel.RData"))return(FALSE)
    load("trainedModel.RData")

if(file.exists("ValueMatrix.RData"))
      load("ValueMatrix.RData")      # Matrix generated by training data is saved

.... Update Matrix based on testing data
save(Matrix,file = "ValueMatrix.RData")

An important reason of raising this question is that, the training data might or might not be changed, which means user could at some point train a model with new data, or still use the previous model if no new data is coming.
We do not want to go through the training process every new session, because when original dataset is large, it might take a long time, and if no new data within a while, we could reuse the model if save to a file.

Appreciate your help!

messages.subject: Re: Execute R code after renderUI()
messages.subject_clean: Execute R code after renderUI()
messages.body_plain:
It is a weird quirk. The problem is that using a selectize input on the second page causes the browser to try to load the JavaScript for selectize from the browser at that time. It loads it in a way that causes the entire browser to block waiting for the JavaScript to be downloaded. But the server is too busy executing your long running task to respond to the download request for the JavaScript file. So the browser is blocked and the server is blocked, and nothing can continue on either side until the server is done executing the long running task. The progress messages are actually being sent to the browser, but the browser isn't paying attention because it's still waiting for the JavaScript.

You can see that this is the case by putting a second selectize input on the first page. This will cause the JavaScript to be loaded right off the bat, and Shiny is smart enough not to load it again when the second page loads.

messages.subject: Re: Per-session object assignment
messages.subject_clean: Per-session object assignment
messages.body_plain:
<<- won't set it for all clients, because the place the variable is declared (flagStem = TRUE) is inside the server function. The <<- operator doesn't automatically assign to the global environment; instead, it will look up the chain of lexical parent environments until it finds a matching variable name, and only if it never finds one does it assign to the global environment.

That being said, I suspect this code can be factored much more "reactively"--alarm bells should go off in your head if you try to assign to outer-scoped variables from within a reactive. Can you say a little more about what you're trying to do here?

On Tue, Oct 27, 2015 at 1:03 PM Yinghao Huang <yingh...@gmail.com> wrote:

>

>   flagStem = TRUE
>
> model <- reactive({
>     modelRes<-NA
>     input$retrain

>         if(isolate({input$stem}) == flagStem)
>              flag = FALSE
>         else flag=TRUE
>         print(paste("Before:",isolate({input$stem}),",",flagStem,",",flag,sep=""))
>         .....
>         flagStem <<- isolate({input$stem})
>         print(paste("After:",isolate({input$stem}),",",flagStem,sep=""))

Hi all, it's been a while since I last posted to this group.  I use shiny quite a bit in my personal projects as it's the only I can make data interactive.  I wanted to show off one of my more recent visualizations:

http://www.sproutworkshop.com/diamond-deals/

I've collected diamond prices from James Allen and calculated the cost-efficiency frontier to find the most cost-effective diamonds.  If you're in the market for an engagement ring or know someone who is, I think this will help you find the best deal online.  I have a lot of fun playing with it to see how different diamonds are priced.  Shiny is the perfect name for a diamond app.

Thanks RStudio, for making this possible.

messages.subject_clean: Change in how reactiveValue works?
messages.body_plain:
New insight into this issue - though I'm still unsure how to properly fix it

The problem seems to be related to having the server functionality build into a package. My current setup is to define a function "server" and then export a function from my package that internally calls runApp(list(server = server, ui = ...)).

Now when I instead create a server.R file in the 'inst' directory of my package containing shiny::shinyServer(PanVizGenerator:::server) (PanVizGenerator being the name of my package) and change the runApp call to runApp(system.file(package='PanVizGenerator')), everything works fine.

I tried to create a minimal example using the list style runApp functionality but couldn't, which leads me to believe that the problem is only relevant when the server function is being exported from a function and the list style is being used...

For now I can use my workaround, but for the sanity of shiny this should be tracked down and fixed - I fear I can't investigate further though...

best

Thomas

What I am doing here is that I have created a checkbox for word stemming. Once I click the input$retrain action button, a model will be trained with/without stemming by calling a topicModel() function. In this function, a term-document matrix is generated and saved.
The logic here is, if user click the train button the second time without changing the stemming checkbox,  the topic model function will skip the matrix generation part and directly use the one that has already been saved.

Yinghao

messages.subject: Re: Per-session object assignment
messages.subject_clean: Per-session object assignment
messages.body_plain:
I think it should be like this.

termDocMatrix <- reactive({
  # calculate something, using input$stem in the process--don't use isolate()
})

model <- eventReactive(input$retrain, {
  # use termDocMatrix() and topicModel() to create and return the model
}, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

Then elsewhere in your app you can refer to model().

See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/action-buttons.html for details on eventReactive, but basically it creates a reactive expression that only invalidates when input$retrain is clicked.

The general idea is that if you want something to be recalculated on a different schedule than something else (in this case, the model and the term document matrix) then they should be in separate reactives. This is the main purpose of reactives: to let derived values be calculated the minimal amount while still maintaining correctness.

messages.body_plain: I am running RStudio on a linux machine I ssh into, and am unable to see any reactive output in the "main panel" in any Shiny App. When I run the example via runExample("01_hello") I get just the sidebar content and main panel title, but no histogram (see attached screenshot). This is consistent across Safari and Chrome,  occurs for Shiny version 0.12.2 and 0.12.0, and is true for all 11 Shiny examples, as well Shiny apps I've written that work on my local machine. I don't see any error messages in my RStudio console. I believe this problem is caused by the old version of R I am running, R 3.1.0. I cannot update my version of R, but wondered if someone could help me come up with a fix to be able to view the reactive output.

Is anyone familiar with such a comparison, or can anyone point to a person or a firm that has substantial experience in this area?
thank you-
MB

messages.subject: Re: Change in how reactiveValue works?
messages.subject_clean: Change in how reactiveValue works?
messages.body_plain:
The workaround (for now):
https://github.com/thomasp85/PanVizGenerator/compare/master...jcheng5:patch-1

This is happening because jquery and shiny.js are both getting loaded twice: once explicitly from a <script> tag in your index.html, and once because Shiny itself didn't realize that you had loaded it. Either one of those getting loaded twice is enough to make behavior in the app pretty unpredictable. In this case, we have a not one but TWO sessions initiated by the same page, and the Generate button is talking to one while the Download button is talking to the other.

I think the fact that both JS libraries are getting loaded twice is something we introduced in either Shiny 0.11 or 0.12. We'll get this fixed right away. Fixing it might mean the above workaround should no longer be used--we'll have to see.

Sorry for the inconvenience!

> On 29 Oct 2015, at 01:15, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

> The workaround (for now):
> https://github.com/thomasp85/PanVizGenerator/compare/master...jcheng5:patch-1
>
> This is happening because jquery and shiny.js are both getting loaded twice: once explicitly from a <script> tag in your index.html, and once because Shiny itself didn't realize that you had loaded it. Either one of those getting loaded twice is enough to make behavior in the app pretty unpredictable. In this case, we have a not one but TWO sessions initiated by the same page, and the Generate button is talking to one while the Download button is talking to the other.
>
> I think the fact that both JS libraries are getting loaded twice is something we introduced in either Shiny 0.11 or 0.12. We'll get this fixed right away. Fixing it might mean the above workaround should no longer be used--we'll have to see.

if(is.null(observerpool$test)) {

        #reactive code etc.
       input$xxx
       ....
       ....
  })
}

--------------server.R -------------------------
# Try to destroy all dynamic observers at a later stage...
isolate({
      obsinst = names(observerpool);
      lapply(obsinst,function(t) {
        obs = eval(parse(text=paste("observerpool$",as.character(t) ,sep="") ))
        if(!is.null(obs)) {
          print(paste("DESTROY() ", as.character(t),sep=""))
          obs$destroy();
          print("Done")
        } else {

      })

messages.subject: Re: remove reactivity
messages.subject_clean: remove reactivity
messages.body_plain:
I don't suppose your app is on GitHub? I'd be very interested in seeing what you're doing.

It sounds to me like maybe you're expecting:

obs <- observe({
  r1 <- reactive(...)
  r2 <- reactive(...)
  output$plot <- renderPlot(... r1() ... r2() ...)
})
obs$destroy()

that the destroy() call would halt the plot and reactive inside. That's not the case.

The main thing I would say is that generally, it's not even close to being worth the effort to "destroy" outputs, reactives, etc. These things take zero computational overhead when they're not executing (though they do hold on to memory if they can't be garbage collected). Shiny assumes that outputs that aren't visible on the page shouldn't be executed and will automatically suspend them. Unless you're actually seeing these outputs unnecessarily executing, or the memory pressure is particularly high, I wouldn't worry about it.

Yesterday I merged a new Shiny Modules feature that you may be interested in. http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html It should simplify the creation of your components. There's nothing that it does to help with destroying modules, but as I noted above I assume that that's not often needed.

You could just make sure that your manual client-side implementation doesn't contain shiny.js or jquery.js references--in fact, it should only contain the contents of <body> (don't even include the <body> tags). And if you want to include things like bootstrap, you can do that using tags$head. Like this:

ui = tagList(
  tags$head(
    tags$script("shared/boostrap.min.js"),  # or whatever
    tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "shared/bootstrap.css")
  ),
  includeHTML("www/index.html")
)

messages.body_plain:
Actually for bootstrap in particular this is better:

bootstrapDependency <- htmltools::htmlDependency("bootstrap", "3.3.1",
        c(
          href = "shared/bootstrap",
          file = system.file("www/shared/bootstrap", package = "shiny")
        ),
        script = c(
          "js/bootstrap.min.js",
          # These shims are necessary for IE 8 compatibility
          "shim/html5shiv.min.js",
          "shim/respond.min.js"
        ),
        stylesheet = if (is.null(theme)) "css/bootstrap.min.css",
        meta = list(viewport = "width=device-width, initial-scale=1")
      )

ui <- htmltools::attachDependencies(includeHTML("www/index.html"), bootstrapDependency)

(Hmmm, ideally we'd let that first big chunk of code be just bootstrapDependency <- shiny::bootstrapDependency. I'll file an issue.)

It's more complicated, but this will prevent bootstrap from getting loaded twice. If you manually put in script/link tags, Shiny doesn't know what you've loaded. The htmlDependency mechanism is a way of declaring CSS/JS dependencies in a way that Shiny can understand.

messages.body_plain:
I was excited to see that the DT team has recently added support for using shift+click to select multiple rows in a datatable (http://editor.datatables.net/examples/simple/multiRow.html). Is there a way to use this feature with shiny-generated datatables?

In a basic example this the one below, multi-selection by clicking on one row at a time works perfectly, but enabling the shift-click behavior isn't as obvious to me.

# app.R
library(shiny)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(fluidRow(column(12, DT::dataTableOutput('tbl')))),
  server = function(input, output) {
    output$tbl = DT::renderDataTable(iris)
  }
)

Thanks!
  - Dan

I noticed that the reference manual for DT has a 'select.style' parameter that closely mirrors the 'selection' parameter of renderDataTable (http://datatables.net/reference/option/select.style). However, setting selection='os' causes termination with the error message "Error in gregexpr(calltext, singleline, fixed = TRUE) : regular expression is invalid UTF-8".

#app.R (this version does not run)
library(shiny)
library(DT)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(fluidRow(column(12, DT::dataTableOutput('tbl')))),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$tbl = DT::renderDataTable(iris, selection='os')
  }
)

#app.R (runs, but no shift-click behavior)
library(shiny)
library(DT)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(fluidRow(column(12, DT::dataTableOutput('tbl')))),
  server = function(input, output) {

    output$tbl = DT::renderDataTable(iris, options=list(select.style='os'))
  }
)

Please let me know if you have any ideas. Thanks!

I don't think this is shiny behaviour, I think the way file inputs in HTML work is that they only fire when they get a new file chosen. messages.subject: Shiny app getting slower (possible reasons: shinyFiles, too many observe parts, ...)
messages.subject_clean: Shiny app getting slower (possible reasons: shinyFiles, too many observe parts, ...)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working on a desktop shiny app (based on  this tutorial: http://www.r-bloggers.com/deploying-desktop-apps-with-r/)
The app is rather big compared to other apps I see on the web and I get the feeling that it got a lot slower in the last few days when I added some more functionality.

Currently I can not share the code but I try to explain it as good as I can:

- sideBarPanel with 2 buttons for loading files, radio buttons, a selectChooser, a custom chooser (exactly this one: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/blob/master/036-custom-input-control/chooser.R), sliderInput, actionButton
- mainPanel with 7 tabs
-> 2 have a data frame displaying loaded files, summaries, ...
-> 1 displays a plot
-> 2 have buttons to load, create, update files
-> 1 displays a result table (data frame)
-> 1 is just used to select to directories

Two things are really slow that bother me:
update* (TextInput, SelectInput, ...) takes a couple of seconds which was not the case before.
The file dialog of shinyFiles is really slow but I like to believe it's not the fault of the package because I would really like to use it.

Overall I use 2 conditional panels (I found this https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/41xS0sCLl3w) but I think 2 should not be the issue.
I have several button+textInput combinations to show the selected file path implemented like this:

  observe({
    if (is.null(input$selectResultPath)) {
      return()
    }

    rootDir<-parseDirPath(volumes, input$selectResultPath)
    updateTextInput(session, 'resultDirPath', value=rootDir)
  })

messages.subject: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
messages.subject_clean: I would need your hints, advices and experience for building bilingual apps.
messages.body_plain:
I've written already some twenty apps of considerable size, almost all of them in Spanish, but I'm considering to include an English
version. I've discarded a second copy with texts in English, because of expected problems in maintenance of two versions. I'd like
to have a language selector in the same app, and swap the texts dynamically.

However, after some tests with an app, complex enough for finding different kind of difficulties, I give up. Inexplicably at least for me,
the two-language version was making its way until a point where it was behaving unpredictably. Some parts (texts or plots) don't
appear but if I refresh the page in the browser (I'm using a remote server, not Rstudio), it can appear complete, perhaps... Even
worse, sometimes the load finishes with an error message, but after refreshing the page loads partially or maybe totally.

I have to explain that this behaviour has not appeared at some critical point. I was advancing slowly, writing small pieces of code
and checking them carefully before facing another piece. The first times I noticed that the error was not a real error I thought that
the reason could be a mismatch between the remote server and my computer, and the upload was not complete when I tried to
refresh the page (it would be strange anyway, since the files are really small).

As I was advancing in the implementation of the two-language version, obviously the program was increasing in complexity. I wonder
if this can have influence in the app behaviour: I had to convert a number of simple p('blablabla'), HTML('blablabla') and widgets in
renderText and renderUI calls (because of the language dependency), BUT it would be hard to accept that functions like that are
able to degrade the program so much.

So I think that I should return to the starting point, and adopt a different paradigm. I've sought a bit about the topic, but it seems
that translations are not very common, or they don't pose any problem normally. In my case, my initial strategy is:
a global environment (.E), with a variable to store the selected language (d): each language has an actionButton, and an observer to update the variable (.E$d)
a global list of character arrays; each array with the expression in English and in Spanish
Examples of use:
  output$titulo = renderText( { .L$titulo[.E$d] } )
  output$par2 = renderUI( { HTML(.L$par2[.E$d]) } )
  output$Type = renderUI({    radioButtons("tipo", .L$pastel[.E$d], c(.L$pie1[.E$d], .L$pie2[.E$d]), inline=TRUE)  })
Perhaps a clue: I'm using withMathJax too. Is it so toxic that it could be related to that undesirable performance?

Have you any similar experience? Can you propose any other strategy? I will appreciate it so much.

JA

messages.body_plain:
Hi José,

I also tried and tried to implement multi linguality in my shiny apps, and i finaly succeed, with, for me, absolutly no loss of performance.

My solution can be tested in an app dedicated to pigeon racing in Belgium. Languages used are English, French (default), and Duch.
You can test it here : http://www.yapluka.be/sapps/beprmap/
Code available here : https://github.com/gvincke/beprmap

My strategy is :
The language will be selected with a select list (takes less place than radio buttons, and is language number independant when wpeeking about layout).
All translated string are in tab separated CSV files, with a column for the id of the string, and as many column as language (fr, en, nl in my example).
These CSV files are imported in server.R in a dataset, and a function (tr for translate) select the right sentence regarding its ID and the current language.
In the github repos you will find this at lines 61 to 64.
So in my app, server.R side, whe i need a translated sentence, i call it with tr("ID").
It works fine, but...
It means that all inputs fields that would have been defined in ui.R are set ups in server.R and called in ui.R with uiOutput()
If you have select list, you will need to charges them regarding the current language, so each multivalue field will need to have its own CSV tanslated file, and setup the field in ui.R (it must exist before sever.R is excuted) but with empty values, and you fill it from server.R with updateSelectInput() function, after having selected all values from the good CSV file. Exemple at line 51 in ui.R and lines 66-78 in server.R.
At my own experience, it's hard to use this with global navigation like navbarPages(), because the language select list can not be set up for all app independently to some panels, so you must set language in only one page, but the field will not be available in others.
In my exemple, the select input is available in the first tab, but not in the other (Credits). So if you are in Credits tab page, and you want to change language, you have to open first tab page, change language, and re-open the Credits page.

I don't know if my exemple helps you, but it works fine for me.

Regards ,

Grégoire

messages.body_plain:
I don't have time at the moment to try to digest Grégoire solution, but I wanted to respond to José's approach:

a global environment (.E), with a variable to store the selected language (d): each language has an actionButton, and an observer to update the variable (.E$d)

This is NOT correct. Instead of an environment you should use reactiveValues(d = defaultLanguage) (where defaultLanguage whatever you decide), and it should not be global, it MUST be located inside the shinyServer function so that it only applies to that session.

a global list of character arrays; each array with the expression in English and in Spanish

That's fine--this can be global. Or better than character arrays, how about a data frame that's read from a .csv? Each row is a string, each column is a language. Then you could use a spreadsheet program to edit the string table (remember to both save and read as UTF-8).

Examples of use:
  output$titulo = renderText( { .L$titulo[.E$d] } )
  output$par2 = renderUI( { HTML(.L$par2[.E$d]) } )
  output$Type = renderUI({    radioButtons("tipo", .L$pastel[.E$d], c(.L$pie1[.E$d], .L$pie2[.E$d]), inline=TRUE)  })

Better to create a wrapper function within the shinyServer function that does this for you, as I believe Grégoire is suggesting.

tr <- function(stringId) {
  .L[[stringId]][.E$d]
}

messages.subject: Suggestion : add for navbarPage() something like navPanel() but inactive
messages.subject_clean: Suggestion : add for navbarPage() something like navPanel() but inactive
messages.body_plain: Hi, I play actually mith the navbarPage() layout, in a exemple of multi language app : French, English, Dutch. The topic is pigeon racing in Belgium. App available here : http://www.yapluka.be/sapps/beprmap/ Code available here : https://github.com/gvincke/beprmap For a pleasant user experience, language must be selectable easely, within every tabs of the app. This is not possible if the select widget is set in a particularly page. If we change of page using one of the tab of the navbar, the select list of available language is lost. The only solution i found is to use the header attribute of navbarPage(), and set the position of this widget using CSS over the navbarPage(). Look at lines 21, 44 and 45 of https://github.com/gvincke/beprmap/blob/master/ui.R This solution works, but is not very cool, because this select list is over the navbar (z-index:1001) and with position absolute to right border of the page. So if the screen gets smaller, the selec list will be placed over tabs. Not cool. My suggestion is that it could be sooo cool if a other kind of tab than tabPanel() can be defined for navbarPage(). A tab wich is not "active" : i mean a li element wich is not inside a link (no tags arround). The aim will be to put there small information like licence, authorship, or widgets. It's exactly the same than the title tab of navbarPage(), so it must'nt be hard to implement. One of the advantage is that this tab will be in the same z-index thant others. Thanks for paying atention to this request. Best regards. Grégoire
